Firstlight - water simulation

2026-11-13 · Stone Age prototype, 64 texture pixels per metre

Flowing river

The river is simulated water: it enters at the top of the map, runs downhill and leaves at the bottom. The surface texture drifts along the real flow direction and speed; shallow water shows the bed.

Real-time, 4 s loop

Spring flood

A flood surge raises the river by about 1.2 m. It spreads over a low floodplain about 8 m wide on each side, then recedes, leaving water standing in hollows. Press F6 in the game to start one.

Time-lapse, each frame = 2 s of game time (about 2.5 minutes in total)
Before · peak · after
MomentWet ground
Before744 cells, about 3,000 m²
Peak1,333 cells, about 5,300 m²
After853 cells, about 3,400 m²

What it does for the game

Water depthWalking
Under about 0.15 mNormal
About 0.15 to 0.65 mWading, 4x slower (fords appear where the river is shallow)
Over about 0.65 mBlocked (deep river; floods cut paths)

Cost: about 0.06 ms per simulation step on the 128 x 128 map, 20 steps per second. Later ages can reuse it for irrigation, wells and dams.

Open question

Should spring floods come every year at a set size, or only some years with a random size?
